title: Access Justification & Attestation Workflow and SIEM Schema
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a pragmatic workflow for attaching access justifications and attestation evidence to RBAC v2 grants, and a lightweight SIEM-friendly audit schema to carry that evidence. The goal: make every high-risk entitlement traceable to a human-reviewed justification, provide timebound attestation metadata, and ensure SIEM ingestion enables both fast alerting and efficient forensic queries without exploding data volume.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to: admin-level grants, cross-tenant delegation, long-lived service principals, and any entitlements flagged as P1/P2 by the Entitlement Risk classifier.
- Not required for ephemeral, low-scope read-only grants (these use existing minimal audit fields).
- We assume downstream SIEM can store structured JSON and supports indexing on a handful of fields (actor, target, entitlement_id, justification_id, attestation_state, retention_bucket).

High-level design
1) Access Justification object: a short, structured justification record created at grant time or retrospectively during attestation. Fields: justification_id (uuid), originator (human or service), purpose_category (one-line enum), narrative (free text, ~200 chars), linked_tickets (list), created_at, expiry_suggested.
2) Attestation lifecycle: periodic reviews where owners confirm/refresh/decline outstanding justifications. Attestation states: pending_review, attested, revoked, escalated_for_deletion. Each change produces a compact evidence event.
3) Evidence envelope: the audit log entry carries a small evidence envelope referencing the justification_id and attestation_state plus a hashed snapshot of the narrative (sha256) to avoid storing long text in hot SIEM indices. Full justification text is kept in the Entitlement Catalog DB (cold storage) and referenced by id for forensics.

SIEM audit schema (minimal event fields)
Each audit event from the authorization layer should include the following top-level keys (names chosen for compatibility with current ingestion):
- event_time: ISO-8601 string (indexable)
- event_type: grant | revoke | attestation_change | access_attempt
- actor_id: internal id for the principal initiating the change (svc- or user-)
- target_resource: resource canonical id (model, dataset, tenant)
- entitlement_id: stable id of the permission (e.g. entitlement:rbac:v2:tenant.update)
- grant_id: uuid for the specific grant instance
- justification_id: uuid or null
- attestation_state: pending_review | attested | revoked | expired | n/a
- justification_hash: sha256 base16 (first 16 chars acceptable for index)
- risk_score: integer 0-100 computed at grant-time
- retention_bucket: short enum (hot_30d | warm_1y | cold_7y) used by downstream storage lifecycle
- op_result: success | failed | partial
- trace_id: trace from request path for correlation

Example event (flattened JSON string stored as message body):
{
  "event_time": "2025-01-20T18:12:33Z",
  "event_type": "grant",
  "actor_id": "user:m.rodiguez",
  "target_resource": "tenant:acme-corp",
  "entitlement_id": "entitlement:rbac:v2:tenant.admin",
  "grant_id": "3f5b8f6a-9e0b-4a2f-a3b2-1d2e9d9b0f1c",
  "justification_id": "jst-202501-44a7",
  "attestation_state": "pending_review",
  "justification_hash": "a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8",
  "risk_score": 82,
  "retention_bucket": "hot_30d",
  "op_result": "success",
  "trace_id": "trace-84b2"
}

Design rationales and tradeoffs
- Keep SIEM index small: only store a short hash of the justification narrative. The full narrative lives in the Entitlement Catalog DB with controlled access. This balances alertability (hash enables quick dedupe/lookup) with privacy and storage cost.
- Retention buckets: downstream systems will use retention_bucket for lifecycle rules. High-risk events default to warm_1y. Enforced by the upload pipeline at event emission time.
- Attestation cadence: default 90 days for high-risk grants, 180 days for medium. Short-lived grants (ttl < 30 days) are auto-marked n/a.
- Risk score: computed by the existing entitlement risk model; stored on grant and used to route evidence to different storage/alerting tiers.

Justification capture UX (practical notes)
- Lightweight creation form for quick grants: pick purpose_category (deploy, incident, maintenance, adhoc-internal, customer-request), paste short narrative, optionally link tickets. Require justification when risk_score >= 60.
- Template text: provide recommended justifications to reduce free-text noise (fewer novel hashes).
- Last-resort grants: an emergency path that flags the grant with emergency=true and requires post-facto attestation within 48 hours.

Attestation orchestration
- Owner assignments: every entitlement_id has an owner (team or person) in the Entitlement Catalog. Owners receive a batched attestation list via email and in-console UI.
- UI vs API attestation: owners can attest via Console or an attestation API. API calls must be signed and emit attestation_change events.
- Escalation: unreviewed pending items older than window escalate to security-on-call and are checkpointed for possible temporary revocation.

Operational runbook (summary)
- Day 0 (launch): enable justification capture for new grants where risk_score >= 50. Emit events to SIEM with retention_bucket set to warm_1y.
- Day 30: start first attestation cycle for grants created in pilot namespace. Monitor attestation completion rate, false positives, and support load.
- Day 60: enable automated escalation for items pending > 14 days in pilot.
- Day 90: widen scope to org-level rollout and adjust risk thresholds based on telemetry.

Forensics and investigations
- Quick triage: SIEM analysts can search by justification_hash to group similar narratives and find associated grants without reading long text.
- Full context: investigators request the Entitlement Catalog record (justification_id) which returns full narrative, linked tickets, and attestation history. Requests are logged and require elevated audit controls.
- Evidence export: create a compact evidence bundle (grant event + attestation history + entitlement snapshot) for legal or compliance needs. Bundle format defined separately.

Data privacy and access controls
- The Entitlement Catalog storing full narratives is access-restricted (RBAC on the RBAC store) and is auditable.
- Hash-only storage in SIEM aims to keep PII/minimal narrative exposure in the central alerting plane.

Open questions and risks
- How to limit narrative verbosity while preserving investigatory usefulness? (Suggest UI character limit + structured tags).
- Exact retention defaults for regulated customers (may require per-tenant overrides).
- SIEM indexing cost: need a cap on cardinality; test with projected hash diversity.

Next steps (action items)
- SEC + Infra: prototype the event envelope and run a 2-week SIEM ingest spike with synthetic events (owner: Ethan Li, due: 2024-12-15).
- DX: small Console UX for justification capture and emergency grant flow (owner: Priya Kapoor, due: 2025-01-10).
- SRE: configure retention lifecycle hooks in the ingest pipeline respecting retention_bucket (owner: Samir Gupta, due: 2025-01-20).
- Legal: review retention and discovery requirements for EU customers (owner: Lena Ortiz, due: 2025-01-05).

Appendix A — Compact evidence event examples
- Attestation change (revoked):
{
  "event_time": "2025-01-20T21:05:00Z",
  "event_type": "attestation_change",
  "actor_id": "user:security-bot",
  "grant_id": "3f5b8f6a-9e0b-4a2f-a3b2-1d2e9d9b0f1c",
  "justification_id": "jst-202501-44a7",
  "attestation_state": "revoked",
  "op_result": "success"
}

- Access attempt denied (high risk):
{
  "event_time": "2025-01-21T10:44:11Z",
  "event_type": "access_attempt",
  "actor_id": "svc:ingest-worker-12",
  "target_resource": "dataset:payments/2024-q4",
  "entitlement_id": "entitlement:data:read:restricted",
  "grant_id": null,
  "justification_id": null,
  "risk_score": 92,
  "op_result": "failed",
  "retention_bucket": "hot_30d"
}

Notes for reviewers
- Please focus review on (1) potential cardinality explosion from justification_hash values, (2) attestation cadence, and (3) compliance implications for per-tenant retention overrides.
- Looking for approval to run the SIEM ingest pilot and shepherd the Console UX.

End of doc
